title: Local descent and uniqueness of the projective cofactor map
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative ring, let $c\geq0$, and let $P,Q$ be finite projective $A$-modules (direct summands of finite free modules [def-weil-pbc-projective-module]) of ranks $c,c+1$ at every prime. Let $u:P\to Q$ be any $A$-linear map, and put $C=Q/u(P)$ and $D_u=(\bigwedge^c_A P)^\vee\otimes_A\bigwedge^{c+1}_A Q$, where $V^\vee=\operatorname{Hom}_A(V,A)$ and exterior powers are [def-weil-pbc-exterior-algebra]. There exists a finite family $f_i\in A$ generating the unit ideal such that $P_{f_i},Q_{f_i}$ are free of these ranks [lem-weil-pbc-finite-projective-standard-free-cover]. The module $J=\bigwedge^c_A P$ is finite projective. For every localization $B=S^{-1}A$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization], the canonical pure-wedge, tensor and dual maps identify $B\otimes_A J$ with $\bigwedge^c_B(B\otimes_A P)$ and $B\otimes_A D_u$ with $(\bigwedge^c_B(B\otimes_A P))^\vee\otimes_B\bigwedge^{c+1}_B(B\otimes_A Q)$. In particular the dual comparison sends $b\otimes\lambda$ to $(b'\otimes x\mapsto bb'\lambda(x))$; these identifications agree under successive localizations.
There is a unique $A$-linear map $w_u:C\to D_u$ with the following property. On any localization $B=S^{-1}A$ on which $P_B$ is free with ordered basis $p_1,\ldots,p_c$, every $v\in Q_B$ satisfies
$$w_{u,B}(\bar v)=(p_1\wedge\cdots\wedge p_c)^\vee\otimes\bigl(u_B(p_1)\wedge\cdots\wedge u_B(p_c)\wedge v\bigr),$$
where $C_B=Q_B/u_B(P_B)$ is identified with $B\otimes_A C$, and $w_{u,B}$ is scalar extension of $w_u$. The right hand side is independent of the basis and the lift $v$. On every finite standard free cover its values on $v/1$, for $v\in Q$, are a matching family in the localizations of $D_u$ and are the localizations of a unique element of $D_u$ [lem-weil-pbc-cover-module-exact]; this characterizes $w_u$ independently of the cover. For $c=0$ it is the canonical identification $Q\cong\bigwedge^1_A Q$ (as $P=0$). The assertions include the zero ring and impose no injectivity on $u$.

source.place: Tag 0E9Y (lemma-determinant), displayed wedge formula and omitted well-definedness check; algebra.tex Tag 00NX (lemma-finite-projective), Tag 00EK (lemma-cover-module), Tags 00DM and 0C6F. Agent-formulated construction for arbitrary differentials, without the source sequence injectivity hypothesis.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-projective-standard-free-cover] separately to $P$ and $Q$. Refine the covers $D(a_i)$ and $D(b_j)$ to $D(a_ib_j)$: the products generate the unit ideal since $1=(\sum r_i a_i)(\sum s_j b_j)$. Bases remain bases after further scalar extension by [lem-weil-pbc-free-base-change-tower]. At a nonzero chart, their lengths are $c,c+1$: localizing a chart basis at any prime preserves its length, and [lem-weil-pbc-finite-projective-rank-locally-constant] identifies this length with the assumed stalk rank. Zero charts have the zero module, which admits a basis of either prescribed length. This yields the asserted common cover.

Choose a splitting $P\xrightarrow{i}A^n\xrightarrow{r}P$, $ri=1$. Applying $i,r$ to each wedge factor gives maps on $c$th exterior powers: multilinearity and the relations $x\wedge x=0$ make them well defined, and their composite is the identity on the spanning pure wedges. Hence $J$ is a direct summand of $\bigwedge^c A^n$, which is finite free by [lem-weil-pbc-exterior-power-free-basis]. Thus $J$ is finite projective. The same argument applies to every exterior power of either $P$ or $Q$, including degree zero.

source.place: Tag 00DM (section-tensor-algebra), alternating relations and finite-free wedge basis; retract argument

proof.text: Apply the exterior and dual comparisons of [lem-trf-projective-exterior-scalar-comparisons] to $P,Q,J$ and $A\to B=S^{-1}A$. Their hypotheses hold by step 2. Combine them with [lem-weil-pbc-localization-tensor-product] for the two factors of $D_u$. This gives exactly the stated identifications of $J_B$ and $(D_u)_B$; the dual comparison evaluates $b\otimes\lambda$ on $b\prime\otimes x$ as $bb\prime\lambda(x)$. The cited scalar-comparison statement includes evaluation and tower compatibility; the tensor comparison multiplies denominators, so it too agrees under successive localizations. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-localization-module-exact] to $P\to Q\to C\to0$ identifies $B\otimes C$ with $Q_B/u_B(P_B)$, by the map $(v+u(P))/s\mapsto v/s+u_B(P_B)$. Surjectivity follows by writing a localized vector as a fraction.

source.place: Tag 0C6F (lemma-tensor-algebra-localization), Tag 00DL (lemma-tensor-product-localization), Tag 00CS (proposition-localization-exact); more-algebra.tex Tag 0FJ9 scalar comparisons

proof.text: On a ring $B$ where $P_B$ has ordered basis $p=(p_1,\ldots,p_c)$, put $e=p_1\wedge\cdots\wedge p_c$. By [lem-weil-pbc-exterior-power-free-basis], $e$ is a basis of $J_B$, with dual $e^\vee$. Define $t_p(v)=e^\vee\otimes(u_B(p_1)\wedge\cdots\wedge u_B(p_c)\wedge v)$. It is linear in $v$. If $v$ is replaced by $v+u_B(x)$, expand $x=\sum a_i p_i$; every extra summand has two identical factors $u_B(p_i)$, hence vanishes. Thus $t_p$ kills $u_B(P_B)$ and descends to the quotient, without requiring injectivity. The same argument covers the empty tuple, whose image is $u_B(0)=0$.

source.place: Tag 0E9Y (lemma-determinant), displayed wedge formula: lift independence and linearity, omitted in the source

proof.text: For another basis $p\prime$ write $p\prime_j=\sum_i g_{ij}p_i$ and $p_j=\sum_i h_{ij}p\prime_i$. Let $a=\sum_{\sigma}\operatorname{sgn}(\sigma)\prod_j g_{\sigma(j),j}$, and define $b$ similarly for $h$. Multilinearity and alternation give $e\prime=ae$, $e=be\prime$, and $u_B(p\prime_1)\wedge\cdots\wedge u_B(p\prime_c)=a(u_B(p_1)\wedge\cdots\wedge u_B(p_c))$: only permutations survive the expansions. Since $e$ is a basis, $ba=1$; consequently $(e\prime)^\vee=be^\vee$. Balancing the tensor cancels $ba$, proving $t_{p\prime}=t_p$. For $c=0$ the permutation sum is $1$. The comparisons in step 3 take these expressions to the same expressions on further localizations; every factor, scalar and dual evaluation has the stated pure-tensor formula.

source.place: Tag 0E9Y (lemma-determinant), omitted basis independence: explicit alternating expansion, also valid in characteristic two

proof.text: Use the finite common cover of step 1. For each $v\in Q$, step 4 gives $t_i(v/1)\in(D_u)_{f_i}$. On $A_{f_if_j}$ the two bases of $P$ give the same value by step 5 and the tower comparisons of step 3. By [lem-weil-pbc-cover-module-exact] this matching family has a unique global value $t(v)\in D_u$. The local equalities $t_i(v+v\prime)=t_i(v)+t_i(v\prime)$ and $t_i(av)=a t_i(v)$ imply the corresponding global equalities, using the injectivity clause of that same node. Likewise $t(u(x))=0$, since its local values vanish by step 4. Thus $t$ factors uniquely through an $A$-linear map $w_u:C\to D_u$. On each chart the localized maps agree on all $v/1$, hence on every $v/f_i^n=f_i^{-n}(v/1)$.

Let $B=S^{-1}A$ be arbitrary with $P_B$ free and choose its basis $p$. The images of the $f_i$ still generate $1$ in $B$. On $B_{f_i}$, the scalar extension of $w_u$ agrees with the formula in the original chart basis by steps 3 and 6. That basis and the localization of $p$ are both bases by [lem-weil-pbc-free-base-change-tower], so step 5 identifies the value with $t_p$. Injectivity in [lem-weil-pbc-cover-module-exact], now over $B$ for the target module, proves equality on $B$. Any other proposed map agrees on the original cover, hence globally by the same injectivity. Any other finite standard free cover gives this same map, so its values glue exactly as claimed. If $c=0$, the rank-zero module $P$ is zero: its chart localizations vanish, and cover injectivity kills every element. Then $C=Q$, $J=A$, and the formula is $v\mapsto1^\vee\otimes v$, the canonical $Q\cong\bigwedge^1Q$: on the free charts this is the degree-one identification of [lem-weil-pbc-exterior-power-free-basis], and the defining tensor quotient gives its global inverse (degree-one tensors map identically to $Q$). The tensor unit removes $A^\vee$. If $A=0$, all modules vanish, and every map and matching family is unique; no prime, nonempty cover, nonzero scalar, or division is required.
